problem: Existing embodied EQA/navigation work treats each goal in isolation with reset memory, and memory-based MLLM agents (3D-Mem, Explore-Mem) store redundant or task-specific data, terminate prematurely on partial exploration, and loop endlessly on infeasible tasks.
motivation: Real-world agents receive sequences of tasks, some infeasible (e.g. non-existent objects), and must reuse spatial knowledge from earlier tasks. MLLMs are overconfident on partial observations and lack explicit geometry, so an external, model-agnostic signal of how much of a space has actually been seen is needed.
key_idea: Use Field-of-View coverage on a 2D grid as an explicit geometric prior to gate memory storage, verify answers/feasibility by room coverage ratio, and score frontiers by unexplored FoV area combined with semantics.
insight: Explicit geometric coverage acts as a calibrated external check that prevents MLLM premature termination and endless re-exploration. Removing the FoV-based mechanisms (3DSPMR w/o Geo) sharply drops results, e.g. GPT-5 EQA SSR 28.2 -> 6.4 and EMN SSPL 27.1 -> 16.2. FoV gating also cuts the number of saved images by 40.8% (EQA) and 30.4% (EMN) versus 3D-Mem.
method: Unified Spatial Memory: three cues — hierarchical 3D scene graph (Apartment/Room/Object; objects via ConceptGraphs, rooms via morphological processing of the occupancy map), a keyframe image bank, and a FoV coverage map, with bidirectional image<->object-node links.
FoV-based gating: ray-cast FoV coverage on a 2D grid; novelty tau = 1 - |C_new ∩ C_hist|/|C_new|; save the frame and update coverage only if tau > tau_0, so memory saturates once explored.
Room coverage rate: eta = |C_hist ∩ S_room|/|S_room| quantifies per-room exploration progress and serves as the termination criterion.
Reasoning Modules (training-free MLLM): Question Analysis, Global Reasoning (prune the scene graph), Local Reasoning (retrieve indexed keyframes), Question Answering.

Geometric Examination: accept an answer only if eta of all task-relevant rooms exceeds a threshold; otherwise trigger exploration. If there is no answer and irrelevant rooms are also covered, label the task infeasible/unanswerable.

Geo-Sem Exploration: frontier score V = w_sem*MLLM semantic relevance + w_exp*(unknown FoV area beyond frontier / max area) + w_dist*1/(1+dist/d_max); pick argmax and go there with the Habitat-Sim shortest-path planner.
SEER-Bench: 48 HM3DSem scenes x 10 tasks (4 infeasible), EQA and EMN tracks, with new episode-level metrics SSR and SSPL.

numbers_note: Custom benchmark (SEER-Bench) and an adapted HM-EQA; no standard official splits, so 'test' is used as the split label. Ablation rows (w/o Geo) exist in the tables but are not listed.
results: 3DSPMR beats the strongest baseline 3D-Mem on all metrics. With GPT-5 on EQA, SSR is 28.2 vs 4.5 and SR 55.9 vs 35.9; on EMN, SSR is 39.6 vs 18.8 and SR 65.0 vs 41.7. It also beats the GOAT-Bench baselines (Modular GOAT SR 24.6), and image memory shrinks by 30-41%.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation on a small benchmark (48 scenes, 240 tasks per track); static environments, with no sim-to-real transfer yet.

Relies on a 2D grid coverage with thresholds and weights and on an accurate occupancy map/pose, and on a proprietary GPT-5 for the best results; absolute SSR on EQA remains low with open models (6.7).
